2) An integration checklist (attached) for networking, API keys, and recommended routing policies.
3) A one-hour technical deep-dive focused on embeddings pipeline and reranker proof-of-concept.

Subject: RE: Post-call: Developer onramp & local SDK run-through for BrightPath — quickstart & local test notes

Hi Liam — quick technical answers and a short local runbook you can share with your engineers.

1) Embedding dims
- The sample pipeline accepts arbitrary vector dims. The vector store layer in the example uses an adaptive indexing shim (you'll see a config value `vector_dim`). If you pass 768 it will work out of the box.

2) Data retention / sandbox vs staging
- Sandbox: ephemeral by default — request/response traces are kept for 24 hours and scrubbed unless you opt-in to longer retention.
- Dedicated staging: configurable retention policy; we can set retention to 0/7/30/90 days per your compliance team. For PII, recommend using client-side tokenization + passing only non-identifying features to the model and enabling encryption at rest on the staging environment.

3) Auth and routing (practical steps)
- Auth options: API keys (simple) or mTLS for private deployments. For hosted sandbox we’ll provide an API key. For Private/VPC we recommend issuing short-lived service tokens via your internal auth broker.
- Routing: set route policy in the config `routes.json` — you can route by latency SLO or by `customer_tier`. For your PoC, use `route: "sandbox"` to keep traffic on the hosted sandbox.

4) Structured output & tool calling
- The SDK includes a `tools` module for deterministic tool invocation patterns (see /examples/tool-calling). Example: tools.use_external_kv(), tools.call_search(). The sample app includes a minimal tool adapter for your triage flow.

5) Local quickstart (Python) — copy/paste to try locally:

pip install redwood-inference-sdk==0.8.1
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<SANDBOX_KEY>"
python -m examples.quickstart.python_run

Inside examples/quickstart/python_run.py you’ll see the basic flow: initialize client, set model variant `redwood-small-v1`, send prompt, and optionally call `client.tools.call("fuzzy_search", {...})`.

6) Local quickstart (TypeScript)

npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<SANDBOX_KEY>"
node examples/quickstart/ts_run.mjs

The TS example shows typed structured output parsing (we emit JSON schema + validation helpers).

7) Embedding + reranker guidance
- Off-the-shelf: generate embeddings via `client.embeddings.create` and store in the included vector store (sqlite wrapper for the sample).
- Reranker: we recommend a two-stage approach — candidate retrieval via nearest neighbors, then rerank with a short-context model. The sample repo includes an L2 candidate fetch + a rerank call using `redwood-reranker-v1`.

Attachments: I uploaded the integration checklist to Drive and included network diagram (attached). Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3CrdIntegrationChecklist, repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-quickstart

If you want, we can make a tiny fork of the sample repo configured for BrightPath (768-dim, example dataset) so your engineers can run with real-ish data during the Thursday call.

Thanks,
—Aditya
